# Yinlong downsi

## claims / statement

<!-- evo:text /records/claims/0/statement -->
Yinlong is anchored by nearly complete holotype IVPP V14530 from the Late Jurassic Shishugou Formation; this specimen-level occurrence is not a global ceratopsian first appearance or a direct ancestor.
<!-- /evo:text -->

## claims / confidenceRationale

<!-- evo:text /records/claims/0/confidenceRationale -->
The holotype and formation are directly documented. High confidence applies to that sample, while basal placement remains a matrix result.
<!-- /evo:text -->

## claims / statement

<!-- evo:text /records/claims/1/statement -->
Yinlong downsi is based on holotype IVPP V14530, and the study recovers the taxon as a basal ceratopsian in its sampled character matrix; that analysis is not evidence of an uncontested relationship or direct ancestry.
<!-- /evo:text -->

## claims / confidenceRationale

<!-- evo:text /records/claims/1/confidenceRationale -->
The holotype and diagnosis are directly documented, whereas its broader placement depends on character scoring, taxon sampling and analysis settings.
<!-- /evo:text -->

## claims / statement

<!-- evo:text /records/claims/2/statement -->
Holotype IVPP V14530 is a nearly complete skeleton missing only the distal tail; the primary description records its broad post-orbital skull region, shallow pre-orbital region and diagnostic cranial features, all limited to the named specimen.
<!-- /evo:text -->

## claims / confidenceRationale

<!-- evo:text /records/claims/2/confidenceRationale -->
The holotype inventory, diagnosis and described cranial anatomy are directly reported and illustrated in the primary study.
<!-- /evo:text -->

## claims / statement

<!-- evo:text /records/claims/3/statement -->
This profile's geographic statement is limited to Wucaiwan in the Junggar Basin, Xinjiang, China, and the upper Shishugou Formation horizon reported for IVPP V14530; it does not establish a global distribution.
<!-- /evo:text -->

## claims / confidenceRationale

<!-- evo:text /records/claims/3/confidenceRationale -->
The locality and horizon are stated directly for the holotype, but one locality-level occurrence cannot establish the genus-wide distribution.
<!-- /evo:text -->

## claims / statement

<!-- evo:text /records/claims/4/statement -->
The primary description estimates the IVPP V14530 individual at about 120 cm and interprets its short forelimbs and robust hindlimbs as compatible with bipedality; diet, habitat preference, guild and observed behaviour are not directly resolved by this anatomy and matrix study.
<!-- /evo:text -->

## claims / confidenceRationale

<!-- evo:text /records/claims/4/confidenceRationale -->
Body proportions and the size estimate are reported for the holotype, while bipedality is an anatomical interpretation and the remaining ecological fields are not direct observations.
<!-- /evo:text -->
